To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the state-covariances of stable linear filters driven by a given signal are canonical, and that this fact can be exploited for spectral estimation purposes.
the state-covariances of linear filters driven by a time series are related to the Toeplitz matrices that are the basis for the MUSIC algorithm.

(i) a new canonical decomposition of the Toeplitz matrix is presented; (ii) this new canonical decomposition is based on the state of the linear filter driven by the time series; (iii) this new decomposition can be exploited to obtain an estimate of the pseudo-spectrum of the time series; and (iv) the resulting pseudo-spectrum has the same form of the MUSIC pseudo-spectrum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method that improves the SNR and is based on the canonical decomposition.
the problem of estimating the spectral lines of a time series by using a stable linear filter.
a new way to estimate a time series that is based on the canonical decomposition and the filtering of the time series.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this new method is a selective harmonic amplification (SHA) technique for spectral analysis of time series.
this method, in contrast to MUSIC, is a true signal estimator, and that the SNR is increased by filtering the process prior to the estimation.
the method presented here is an alternative way to obtain pseudo- spectra that highlight the spectral- energy distribution of a time-series, but with the advantage of improving the SNR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is an improvement of MUSIC, in that it is able to detect weak signals that are not visible in the original data.
the new method is a selective harmonic amplification (SHA) technique that is capable of retrieving spectral lines from time series with low SNR.
we are able to improve the performance of MUSIC by filtering the time series before applying the canonical decomposition of MUSIC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the canonical decomposition of a stable filter is a powerful tool to extract information from a time series.
the canonical decomposition of a state-covariance is a useful tool to obtain information on the spectral lines of a time series, even when the SNR is low.
the new method, called selective harmonic amplification (SHA), can be used to obtain pseudo-spectrum that highlight the spectral distribution of the process, even if the SNR is very low.
